stories.title: Spain high‑speed train crash kills 69 weeks before snap election
stories.summary: A collision on the high‑speed rail line south of Madrid resulted in 69 bodies being recovered from wreckage strewn across the tracks and down an embankment in central Spain. The disaster occurs weeks before the snap general election called by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who is already facing public anger over alleged corruption and housing costs, and a formal investigation into the earlier Toledo train disaster has just been launched.
stories.why: The incident may influence public confidence in the rail system and the government ahead of the election.

stories.title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
stories.summary: A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis. xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile.

stories.title: Nifty rebounds 2% but faces resistance near 23,450
stories.summary: The Nifty index rose 2% last week, moving back above its 200‑week moving average of 22,700. Analysts see immediate resistance between 23,300 and 23,450 and key support in the 22,750‑22,525 range for the upcoming week. Easing volatility and buying at lower levels underpin the rebound, though bearish momentum indicators call for caution. Trending stocks include SBI, Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, Infosys, Wipro and NTPC.
stories.why: The identified support and resistance zones will guide short‑term trading decisions for market participants.

stories.title: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia
stories.summary: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia, The Information reported Thursday . Anthropic’s contract with Nscale covers the first 460-megawatt building at Nscale’s West Virginia campus, which is expected to use Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin chips.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.
stories.previousTitle: Nvidia in talks to co‑sign debt for Nscale’s West Virginia AI data center
stories.previousSummary: Nvidia is discussing a residual‑value guarantee that would back billions of dollars in debt financing for Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia. The arrangement would let Nscale secure funding for construction and electricity costs, with Nvidia stepping in if Nscale defaults, temporarily taking control of the facility and helping find a buyer or new tenant. Anthropic has a $44.6 billion contract for the first 460‑MW building, and a second deal of roughly $45 billion is being discussed.
